_README: Per-source blaze mapping tables (#782, features/NEARBY_TRAILS.md section 4).
A reviewed file, the shelter_capacity.json posture: every row is somebody's
decision that a raw source value IS a particular paint on a tree, and
reviewing a diff of this reviews those decisions. That is the whole reason
it is committed rather than derived.
THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO ENFORCE
The maintainer's decision (2026-08-18): 'the color of the trail blazes
should be the color on the map', and 'some way to stop sprawl is needed'.
The palette in client/src/lib/blaze.ts is closed and grows by review. This
is the other half: every source normalizes INTO that palette, and a value
with no row here falls to Unknown neutral with a loud warning. A color the
map has never heard of must never invent a paint.
`mapped` names a palette member. `deferred` records a value we have SEEN
and decided not to paint yet, with the reason and what would settle it -
the distinction matters, because a deferred value is a decision and an
absent one is an oversight, and they render identically. lib/blaze.py
warns differently for each, which is what makes the difference visible.
Counts are from the #771 spike against OPRHP's statewide layer, measured
2026-08-18. Nothing OPRHP-derived publishes until #769 records their
licence answer; this file is the machinery, not the release.

_note: New York State Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation,
statewide trails layer. Carries Blaze/Blaze_2/Blaze_3 plus Map_Blaze.

Light Blue.why: A real distinct paint in these parks rather than a spelling of Blue, so collapsing it onto Blue would flatten two trails a hiker tells apart at a junction. Wants its own palette member.
Light Blue.settles_it: An admission review: a hex that clears the bars in client/src/lib/blaze.ts next to both Blue and Aqua, which is the crowded corner of this palette.

Pink.why: The largest unmapped count, and no existing member is honestly near it. Not a spelling of Red or Purple.
Pink.settles_it: An admission review. Nothing about it is ambiguous except that nobody has picked a hex.

Brown.why: Nearest existing members are the neutral grey and Purple, and neither is brown. Painting it as either would be confidently wrong.
Brown.settles_it: An admission review, with attention to the day sheet - brown on tan contours is the pairing that would fail an outdoor pass (#105).

Black.why: Real paint, and the one candidate the neutral fallback's own design argues against: TRAIL_BLAZE_COLORS.md says the fallback 'cannot be black, near-black, or anything close to the 8 real hues'. Admitting Black needs that sentence revisited, not just a hex.
Black.settles_it: A decision about whether Black-on-dark-sheet is drawable at all, ahead of a hex.

Lime.why: The smallest count, and the one most likely to be a spelling of Green rather than a separate paint. Mapping it onto Green without checking would merge two trails; giving it a member without checking would split one.
Lime.settles_it: Reading a sample of Lime segments against their trails' published blaze descriptions - measurement before mapping, per the design doc.
